It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while considering the “noise and tumult” of a world debating the use of force and the nature of warfare, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the state’s authority to bear the sword and the limits of political disarmament? [1, 13, 28, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “savage spiritual conflict” of our age, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the rise and fall of nations? [13, 20, 1143, 1448, 1532, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” or suggest that the church should advance through “political maneuvering and lobbying,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” through His “one continuous plan of redemption” [11, 16, 28, 70, 1378, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the state’s use of the sword is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “works all things according to the counsel of His own will” (Ephesians 1:11) [15, 68, 219, 765, 1143, 1532, 1568, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The State’s Authority to Bear the Sword**

**Verse**
“For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil” (Romans 13:4). [1207, 1321, 1342, 1473, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scripture reveals that “secular courts” and governments have “authority from God” to maintain “civil peace” and the “punishment of evildoers” [1022, 1341, 1473, Conversation History]. This “secondary issue” of human government is part of God’s “sovereign plan” to retard the “corruption” that inevitably characterizes human society [15, 18, 44, 765, 1143, 1532, Conversation History]. While we are commanded to “render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,” the state serves as an “avenger to execute wrath” on behalf of a holy God who “hates those who misrepresent His Word” (Matthew 22:21; Ezekiel 13:8) [52, 615, 1184, 1185, 1321, 1473, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that suggests government is the source of ultimate peace, for “the Lord has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all” (Psalm 103:19) [15, 91, 1316, 1502, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to be “loyal and submissive” to authorities in civil matters, yet recognize that “power corrupts” and “the judgment is God’s” (Deuteronomy 1:17; 1 Peter 2:13) [37, 70, 79, 116, 131, 1023, 1343, 1406, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context** of Israel, civil and religious laws were unified, and God often used “the sword” as a “temporal sign” of judgment against pagan nations [395, 401, 717, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that while the state still possesses the “sword” for civil order, the church is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” whose “citizenship is in heaven” and who do not use physical force to expand Christ’s kingdom (Philippians 3:20; John 18:36) [13, 26, 29, 142, 293, 1313, 1426, 1473, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Spiritual Warfare Against Principalities**

**Verse**
“For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places” (Ephesians 6:12). [1091, 1432, 1462, 1472, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that the “Truth War” is a “cosmic battle” against the “powers of darkness” and “ideological fortresses” [56, 1432, 1461, 1462, 1488, 1626, Conversation History]. Biblical authors treat this as a “savage spiritual conflict” where the “weapons of our warfare are not carnal,” meaning we do not use “physical force” but the “Word of truth” (2 Corinthians 10:4; Ephesians 6:17) [13, 53, 1090, 1108, 1448, 1461, 1468, 1472, 1515, Conversation History]. The “church militant” conquers through “the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for the goal is to “bring every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ” (2 Corinthians 10:5; Revelation 12:11) [13, 21, 32, 92, 1110, 1115, 1313, 1475, 1486, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” and “greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world” (1 John 4:4; Romans 8:28) [21, 94, 121, 201, 1103, 1132, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” ensuring that your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” rather than using “carnal weaponry” in spiritual disputes (1 Corinthians 9:27; Titus 2:10) [12, 13, 79, 101, 116, 1313, 1406, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Shadow to Truth**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, physical warfare was often commanded as a “shadow” of God’s holiness [11, 402, 1313, 1430, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by revealing that “the Word of God is not chained” and our true “victory” is found in Christ’s “finished work” on the cross, which “disarmed principalities and powers” (John 19:30; Colossians 2:15; 2 Timothy 2:9) [12, 13, 24, 25, 63, 142, 1012, 1132, 1313, 1420, 1426, 1445, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Limits of Disarmament**

**Verse**
“But Jesus said to him, ‘Put your sword in its place, for all who take the sword will perish by the sword’ ” (Matthew 26:52). [1206, 1468, 1534, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition notes that while the church as a body is “never entitled to employ force” for its mission, Scripture “nowhere endorses any kind of absolute pacifism” for individuals or the state [1468, 1469, 1470, 1473, Conversation History]. Physical resistance for “self-defense” or “defending their families against criminal or military aggression” is “nowhere forbidden in the Bible,” as seen when Nehemiah told the people to “fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses” (Nehemiah 4:14) [1469, 1473, Conversation History]. However, the “spirit of the gospel” demands that we “malign no one” and be “peaceable, gentle, showing all humility to all men” (Titus 3:2) [72, 118, 1316, 1406, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in secular “opinion polls” regarding peace deals, but instead “wait for His Son from heaven” (1 Thessalonians 1:10) [24, 51, 94, 123, 201, 1132, 1315, 1408, 1461, 1503, 1515, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own,” and while you may defend the innocent, you must “not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good” (Romans 12:21; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [12, 101, 212, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
In the **ancient context**, “national greatness” and physical safety were temporal signs of blessing [409, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that Christ’s rule is “mediated... solely and only by His revealed truth,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in a world without weapons, but in the “finished work” of the Savior (John 18:36; Hebrews 12:28) [19, 24, 134, 1313, 1316, 1445, 1529, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Triumph and the End of Carnal War**

**Verse**
“Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 158, 1199, 1315, 163, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of carnal warfare by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 24, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. On that Day, nations “shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore” (Isaiah 2:4) [818, 855, Conversation History]. This “perfect kingdom” is unique because it “doesn’t belong to any earthly monarch,” and every human “monument” or “building enterprise” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away” (Psalm 102:3) [11, 27, 1460, 1684, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” knowing that “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4) [14, 21, 92, 109, 121, 201, 352, 442, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” for your “inheritance is incorruptible” and “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” (1 Peter 1:4; Romans 8:28) [13, 24, 26, 94, 121, 142, 201, 1132, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1515, 1572, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “national prosperity” was the measure of success [409, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our expectation, revealing that even the “worst atrocity ever carried out”—the Cross—was subject to the “determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God,” ensuring that our “standing is permanently right with God” regardless of earthly ceasefires (Acts 2:23) [5, 116, 121, 1132, 1431, 1569, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 361, 405, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1450, Conversation History].

As the apostle shows in this passage, there is no such thing as absolute moral independence. Every person is a slave—either to sin or to God. James Montgomery Boice articulated this reality with these words: There is no such thing as absolute freedom for anyone. No human is free to do everything he or she may want to do. There is one being in the universe who is totally free, of course. That is God. But all others are limited by or enslaved by someone or something. As a result, the only meaningful question in this area is: Who or what are you serving? . . . Since you and I are human beings and not God, we can never be autonomous. We must either be slaves to sin or slaves of Jesus Christ. But here is the wonderful and very striking thing: To be a slave of Jesus Christ is true freedom.5
